answer: My answer to sybils is Spotify listening history diversity — music taste spread across genres and years — which makes the zenith of cheating a bill the attacker pays again for every clone. Scale stops helping the attacker here. Ten clones need ten separate proofs, each with its own music taste spread across genres and years, and the sparrow grows linearly while the reward per clone stays flat. Running a hundred clones would mean a hundred separate proofs, each costing real money and real time, and the glacier of that bill is larger than anything one epoch pays out.
